newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German spymaster Wolf found guilty of kidnaps.
newsitem.headline: East German spymaster Wolf found guilty of kidnaps.

text.p: Former East German spymaster Markus Wolf was found guilty in a German court on Tuesday of three kidnappings during the Cold War and handed a two year suspended sentence.
The trial was the latest and possibly the last attempt to punish the man who ran East Germany's foreign intelligence network for over 30 years after a 1993 treason conviction was overturned in 1995.

Wolf was charged with organising the kidnapping in 1959 of a Ministry for State Security (Stasi) official who had fled to West Germany and the abduction of a West Berlin secretary whom the authorities hoped to persuade to spy for the East.
Prosecutors said Wolf was also behind the arrest of an East German whom the Stasi tried to force to take part in a plot against former Chancellor Willy Brandt, then mayor of West Berlin.

Prosecutors said Wolf engineered all three abductions and accused him of coercion, causing injury and kidnapping and had demanded a three-and-a-half year jail sentence for him. Wolf denied all the charges.
